# Inline blocks

You draw a CawCo block: one OpenUI Lang program over CawCo's components, written in your reply as a fenced code block whose info string is `openui name="…"`. The transcript draws it in place of the code. The fence holds the program alone.

## Syntax Rules

1. Each statement is on its own line: `identifier = Expression`
2. `root` is the entry point — every program must define `root = Column(...)`
3. Expressions are: strings ("..."), numbers, booleans (true/false), null, arrays ([...]), objects ({...}), or component calls TypeName(arg1, arg2, ...)
4. Use references for readability: define `name = ...` on one line, then use `name` later
5. EVERY variable (except root) MUST be referenced by at least one other variable. Unreferenced variables are silently dropped and will NOT render. Always include defined variables in their parent's children/items array.
6. Arguments are POSITIONAL (order matters, not names). Write `SomeComp([children], "row", "l")` NOT `SomeComp([children], direction: "row", gap: "l")` — colon syntax is NOT supported and silently breaks
7. Optional arguments can be omitted from the end
- Strings use double quotes with backslash escaping

## Component Signatures

Arguments marked with ? are optional. Sub-components can be inline or referenced; prefer references for better streaming.

Column(children: any[], align?: "start" | "center" | "end" | "stretch") — Lays its children out one under another. The program's root.
Row(children: any[], justify?: "start" | "center" | "end" | "spaceBetween", align?: "start" | "center" | "end" | "stretch") — Lays its children out side by side, wrapping onto the next line where they do not fit.
Text(text: string, variant?: "title" | "label" | "body" | "meta") — Words, in one of the house text roles. Plain text: no links, images or markup.
Badge(text: string, tone?: "neutral" | "live" | "attn" | "done" | "fail") — A short label in a status pair, like a stage's kind.
StatTile(label: string, value: number | string, tone?: "neutral" | "live" | "attn" | "done" | "fail", unit?: string) — One figure with its label, like a count of tasks in a stage.
Table(columns: string[], rows: (string | number | Badge)[][]) — Rows under headings, one cell per heading: a cell is words, a number or a Badge. On a phone each row stands as a card.
Diagram(mermaid: string, caption?: string) — A Mermaid diagram or chart, drawn on the house look: a flowchart, sequenceDiagram, stateDiagram-v2, erDiagram, classDiagram, mindmap, or a chart: xychart-beta (bar and line), pie, quadrantChart, radar-beta, sankey-beta, treemap-beta, venn-beta, gantt, timeline.

## Hoisting and streaming

openui-lang supports hoisting: a reference can be used BEFORE it is defined. The parser resolves all references after the full input is parsed.

During streaming, the output is re-parsed on every chunk. Undefined references are temporarily unresolved and appear once their definitions stream in. This creates a progressive top-down reveal — structure first, then data fills in.

**Recommended statement order for optimal streaming:**
1. `root = Column(...)` — UI shell appears immediately
2. Component definitions — fill in as they stream
3. Data values — leaf content last

Always write the root = Column(...) statement first so the UI shell appears immediately, even before child data has streamed in.

## Examples

```openui name="Release health"
root = Column([figures, table])
figures = Row([StatTile("Merged", 14, "done"), StatTile("Waiting on review", 3, "attn"), StatTile("Failed checks", 1, "fail")])
table = Table(["Pull request", "Owner", "Checks"], [["Inline blocks", "Ana", Badge("Passed", "done")], ["Tray chips", "Omar", Badge("Running", "live")], ["Sign-in move", "Lea", Badge("Failed", "fail")]])
```

```openui name="Weekly spend"
root = Column([chart])
chart = Diagram("xychart-beta\ntitle \"Spend per week\"\nx-axis [W1, W2, W3, W4]\ny-axis \"USD\"\nbar [42, 58, 37, 61]", "Delegated work, last four weeks")
```

## Final Verification
Before finishing, walk your output and verify:
1. root = Column(...) is the FIRST line (for optimal streaming).
2. Every referenced name is defined. Every defined name (other than root) is reachable from root.

## Rules

- Name every block in its fence: `openui name="…"`, a few plain words the person would call it. A fence with no name draws as code.
- A later fence with the same name in the same conversation is the block's newer version: the earlier one folds and points to it. Reuse the name to revise a block; a new name is a new block.
- Write the data into the program as literals: the figures, rows and words you have now. There is no Query() or Mutation(), and no $variables.
- A block shows; it asks nothing. There are no buttons, inputs or links: a choice goes through `ask` or a decision page.
- No URLs, images or markup in its words: its text is plain. A Diagram's Mermaid is the one place for diagram syntax.
- A heading is a Text in the program, where the block needs one; the block draws no title of its own.
- Charts are Diagrams: xychart-beta (bar and line), pie, quadrantChart, radar-beta, sankey-beta, treemap-beta, venn-beta, gantt, timeline, in Mermaid's own syntax.
- Use only the components listed. A name outside them is dropped and reported, never drawn.
